odd_even_pairs.option: form: picture of up to 20 objects to pair up, and "write the even number as a double" (14 = 7 + 7)
odd_even_pairs.name: Odd or Even by Pairing (option)
odd_even_pairs.teaches: deciding odd or even by pairing objects or counting in 2s, and writing an even number as a sum of two equal addends
odd_even_pairs.representation: pair the objects: odd or even?; count in 2s to decide; write 14 = 7 + 7; which number is a double?
odd_even_pairs.why: existing STANDARD_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
odd_even_pairs.closes: R.B9.S6: pairing objects to see whether one is left over; R.B11.S13: pairing objects to see odd and even

doubles_pictured.option: pictures: two equal rows, totals to 8 / 10
doubles_pictured.name: Doubles with Pictures (option)
doubles_pictured.teaches: find the double in a picture of two equal groups, or draw the matching group to make a double; write the total (to 8, then to 10)
doubles_pictured.representation: two identical rows of counters in one boxed cell; write the total
doubles_pictured.closes: R.B9.S7: recognising a double (two equal groups) pictured, totals to 8; R.B9.S8: making a double with objects to 8; R.B11.S11: recognising a pictured double to 10; R.B11.S12: making a double with objects to 10; R.B16.S6: playing with and building doubles with objects

time_talk.name: Time Words
time_talk.teaches: the language of time (today, yesterday, tomorrow, days of the week, months, seasons, before, after)
time_talk.representation: calendar strip or picture timeline; circle or write the word from a bank
time_talk.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
time_talk.closes: R.B10.S5: time language: now, before, after, morning, night, yesterday, tomorrow

compare_small.name: Compare Numbers to 10 and 20 (option)
compare_small.teaches: comparing and ordering numbers and groups of objects within 10 and 20 (and tens-and-ones pictures to 100) with <, >, = and the words greater than / less than / equal to (the lowest band today is 99)
compare_small.representation: band options 10 and 20 on placevalue:compare and the two order skills, a ten-frame or tens-and-ones picture support level
compare_small.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
compare_small.closes: R.B11.S2: comparing two numerals to 10 (not groups) with more / fewer

bonds_3_parts.name: Bonds to 10 in Three Parts (option)
bonds_3_parts.teaches: split a whole of 10 into three parts and write the missing part
bonds_3_parts.representation: part-whole diagram, one whole and three part circles
bonds_3_parts.why: number_bonds has two parts only; add_three is an addition fact, not a part-whole
bonds_3_parts.closes: R.B11.S10: bonds to 10 in three parts

shape_3d_tasks.name: What Can This Shape Do?
shape_3d_tasks.teaches: properties of 3-D shapes in use: roll, stack, slide; flat and curved faces; faces seen in 3-D shapes
shape_3d_tasks.representation: line drawings of 3-D shapes; tick roll/stack/slide; match the face print to the 3-D shape
shape_3d_tasks.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
shape_3d_tasks.closes: R.B12.S2: finding the flat (2-D) faces on 3-D shapes; R.B12.S3: choosing a 3-D shape for a job (it rolls, it stacks); R.B15.S1: selecting a shape for a purpose; R.B15.S8: finding 2-D faces within 3-D shapes

teen_bands.name: Teen Number Bands (option)
teen_bands.teaches: build and continue only the numbers of the step: 10-13, 14-16 or 17-20
teen_bands.representation: the skill's own ten-frame cell, numbers held to the band
teen_bands.why: the bands are 15 and 19 (11-15, 11-19), which overreach each WRM step and never reach 20
teen_bands.closes: R.B13.S1: building 10, 11, 12 and 13 only; R.B13.S2: continuing the count 10, 11, 12, 13 only; R.B13.S3: 14 to 20, with 20 as two full tens (the band stops at 19 and starts at 11)

teen_structure.name: Understand 10 and 20 (option)
teen_structure.teaches: 10 as one ten and 20 as two tens (the skill covers 11-19)
teen_structure.representation: band values "exactly 10" and "20" on teen_compose with one and two full ten frames
teen_structure.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
teen_structure.closes: R.B13.S3: 14 to 20, with 20 as two full tens (the band stops at 19 and starts at 11)

oral_count.name: Count Aloud Track (option)
oral_count.teaches: point to each number on a track and say it, past 20 and across a decade; the teacher ticks the numbers said
oral_count.representation: a long number track (to 30 or 100) with tick boxes under it; no writing
oral_count.why: the steps are oral; the live skill checks only written gaps
oral_count.closes: R.B13.S5: oral counting past 20 (the written track is the only check); R.B13.S6: saying the counting pattern and noticing that 1-9 repeat in every decade

pictures_change_unknown.option: unknown: change (the same option on subtraction:sub_5_pictures); within 5
pictures_change_unknown.name: How Many Were Added / Taken Away? (option)
pictures_change_unknown.teaches: look at the before and after pictures and write how many were added, or how many were taken away (within 5)
pictures_change_unknown.representation: a before box and an after box of counters in one cell; write the change
pictures_change_unknown.why: the picture skills ask only for the result; one change only (no band lift: P-1, and the skills are named "within 5")
pictures_change_unknown.closes: R.B14.S2: change unknown: how many were added; R.B14.S4: change unknown: how many were taken away

defining_attributes.name: Is It Still a Triangle?
defining_attributes.teaches: defining attributes (closed, number of straight sides, corners) versus non-defining attributes (colour-free: size, orientation, thickness of line)
defining_attributes.representation: is it still a triangle when turned / bigger / thinner?; which of these are triangles? (open shapes, curved sides); what makes it a square? tick; sort: changes the shape / does not
defining_attributes.why: existing STANDARD_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
defining_attributes.closes: R.B15.S2: recognising a turned shape as the same shape

scenes.name: Copy and Build
scenes.teaches: copying a picture or construction made of shapes, visualising from another viewpoint, replicating a scene
scenes.representation: a model picture made of shapes beside an empty frame; draw or choose the matching copy
scenes.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
scenes.closes: R.B15.S4: describing how shapes are arranged; R.B15.S7: copying a picture made of 2-D shapes; R.B17.S4: replicating a scene or construction from a model; R.B17.S5: visualising objects from different positions

decompose_shapes.name: Find the Shapes Inside (option)
decompose_shapes.teaches: look at a shape cut by lines and say which smaller shapes make it (two triangles make a square)
decompose_shapes.representation: one shape with its cut lines drawn; tap or circle the parts from a choice of shapes
decompose_shapes.why: compose_shapes only puts two shapes together
decompose_shapes.closes: R.B15.S6: decomposing a shape into smaller shapes

share_group.name: Share and Make Groups
share_group.teaches: sharing a small amount equally (one for you, one for me) and grouping into equal groups within 10, including odd amounts that do not share fairly
share_group.representation: counters drawn next to plates or rings; draw them shared or grouped; write how many each / how many groups; option: fair or not fair
share_group.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
share_group.closes: R.B16.S1: exploring sharing an amount fairly; R.B16.S2: sharing one by one between a given number (how many each); R.B16.S3: exploring making equal groups; R.B16.S5: odd and even through sharing between two

consolidate.name: Number Sense Review
consolidate.teaches: consolidating counting, cardinality, composition and patterns to 10 (Reception year review)
consolidate.representation: a mixed page of counting, compare, compose and pattern cells drawn from the existing K skills (a review pool, not new content)
consolidate.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
consolidate.closes: R.B18.S1: a consolidation review across the Reception year; R.B18.S2: number relationships (1 more, doubles, bonds) reviewed together
